changelog: Insert a single fallback ordering after C8: as a last resort prefer punctuation/clause-boundary cuts over cuts that split a numeral from its unit/measurement or that separate a finite verb/auxiliary from its immediately following core complement—implements the required fallback order (addresses the primary finding about numerals) without adding a prohibition.
findings: The prompt undervalues cuts that separate a finite verb or auxiliary from the phrase that completes its core predicate (object, prepositional complement, clausal complement or essential continuation), causing contradictory or incoherent fragments when pieces are translated separately.

The prompt fails to protect numeral/measurement units: it allows cuts that split a numeral or quantifier from its unit or adjacent parenthetical measurement, which breaks numeric meaning or produces misleading fragments.

edits.was: - Does the stretch after the cut supply disambiguating information (names, numbe
edits.now: - As a last resort, prefer a cut at a punctuation or clause boundary (comma, sem

diagnosis.why: Inserting the fallback that prefers punctuation/clause-boundary cuts as a last resort made the model favor clause/punctuation boundaries more often, producing a small net improvement concentrated on short pieces (largest gains in the ≤3 and ≤5 bins) but also shifting many kept cuts so they now split numerals/units or separate finite verbs from their immediately following complements, which explains the sizable set of worse (but more localized) degradations.
diagnosis.lesson: A later revision should keep the punctuation/clause-boundary preference that helped short pieces while ensuring it does not override protections that keep numerals attached to their units or finite verbs attached to their core complements.
